主要内容: On May 6, 2020, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced a $96 billion issuance of Treasury securities to refund $57 billion in privately-held notes and bonds maturing on May 15, 2020. This move would raise approximately $39 billion in new cash. The securities include a $42 billion 3-year note, a $32 billion 10-year note, and a $22 billion 30-year bond, all maturing on May 15, 2023, 2030, and 2050, respectively. The auctions for these securities will occur on May 11, 12, and 13, 2020, with settlements on May 15. The Treasury also plans to increase auction sizes for longer-dated notes and floating-rate notes over the May-to-July quarter, while keeping TIPS auction sizes unchanged. This reflects the increased borrowing needs due to the federal government's response to the COVID-19 outbreak. The U.S. Department of the Treasury announced its quarterly refunding statement on May 6, 2020, detailing plans to increase the size of various auction programs. The 7-year note auction will increase by $9 billion by the end of July, with $3 billion per month over the next three months. The 10-year and 30-year note auctions will also see increases of $5 billion and $3 billion, respectively, starting in May. The FRN auction sizes will increase by $2 billion for May and June reopenings, resulting in a $20 billion auction size for each. The Treasury also plans to issue a 20-year nominal coupon bond with an initial offering size of $20 billion, set to auction on May 20, 2020. The Treasury anticipates that these changes will result in an additional $154 billion in issuance to private investors during the May-July quarter compared to the February-April quarter. Additionally, the Treasury will continue to supplement its regular bill financing with CMBs and maintain TIPS issuance sizes at specified levels. The U.S. Department of the Treasury issued a quarterly refunding statement on May 6, 2020, outlining plans to release a Request for Information (RFI) to better understand potential demand for a new security and how it could align with the Treasury’s long-term goal of financing the government at the lowest cost. The RFI is expected to be released in May 2020, and the Treasury encourages market participants and the public to provide feedback. Additionally, the Treasury plans to conduct a small-value test auction using its contingency auction system sometime over the next three months. This test is not intended to signal any changes to existing auction processes. The next quarterly refunding announcement is scheduled for August 5, 2020.
